rationale: Evidence from iteration 0: every development trial on all three tracks ended off_track (60 of 60 runs). Progress stalled at 0.11 to 0.15, and max_error sat at about 0.06 m, which is the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.12/4) = 0.06). The robot is not failing through jitter, since steering_oscillation is small (0.07 to 0.14). It is failing by drifting off the line on bends and never recovering. The most likely causes are (1) base_speed 1.6 is too fast for the steering to follow the tape through the bends, and (2) kd 0.3 gives too little damping, so the correction overshoots. Changes: base_speed reduced from 1.6 to 1.3 to give the steering more time per bend. kp raised slightly from 3.0 to 3.5 for a firmer correction, and kd raised from 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the overshoot. ki is cut to 0.01 to avoid integral windup on the longer runs. The sensor spread is tightened to x = -0.03 to +0.03 m and moved forward to y = 0.04 m, so the sensors read the line closer to the axle with less lag. Mass is reduced to 0.7 kg so the yaw inertia falls and the robot turns more easily. The other geometry is kept unchanged. Expected result: fewer off-track ends, with some runs finishing or progressing much further (progress above 0.5). Completion time may get longer because of the lower speed, so the finish is not yet guaranteed. Hypotheses to test: (a) if the runs still leave on the sharpest bends, kp needs to go up or base_speed down further; (b) if steering_oscillation rises above about 0.5, kd is too high; (c) if line_loss_events are above 1, the sensors are losing the tape at the edges and the spread needs widening. Next measurements: progress, completion, max_error and rms_error on each track, plus steering_oscillation and line_loss_events, so I can see where the robot leaves the line.
